problem.summary: 实时目标检测在速度与精度之间存在权衡，且现有方法在训练优化（如模型重参数化、动态标签分配）中面临新问题。

motivation.summary: 随着目标检测方法的发展，模型重参数化和动态标签分配等训练技术产生了新的研究课题，需要新的方法来解决这些问题，同时提升实时检测器的性能。

core_idea.summary: 提出可训练的“免费工具包”（trainable bag-of-freebies）方法，结合灵活高效的训练工具、新架构和复合缩放方法，在不增加推理成本的情况下显著提高检测精度。

method.summary: 设计扩展高效层聚合网络（E-ELAN）架构、计划重参数化模型、粗到细引导标签分配等训练优化技术，并提出针对连接型模型的复合缩放方法。

experiments.summary: 在MS COCO数据集上从头训练，与多种实时检测器（如YOLOv5、YOLOX、PPYOLOE、YOLOR等）和基于Transformer的检测器进行对比，并进行多项消融研究。

claims.claim: YOLOv7在5 FPS到160 FPS范围内超越所有已知目标检测器的速度和精度；在30 FPS或更高帧率的实时检测器中达到最高精度56.8% AP；提出的可训练免费工具包方法能有效提升检测精度。
YOLOv7-E6在速度和精度上显著优于基于Transformer的检测器（如Swin-L Cascade-Mask R-CNN）。
提出的复合缩放方法在连接型模型上比单独缩放宽度或深度更有效。
计划重参数化模型能避免恒等连接破坏残差或连接操作，提升模型性能。
粗到细引导标签分配方法优于独立标签分配和引导标签分配。
部分辅助头能弥补下一级金字塔预测可能丢失的信息，进一步提升性能。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论方法的局限性，但实验主要基于MS COCO数据集，未涉及其他数据集或领域；部分实现细节（如具体超参数）未完全公开。

nodes.title: 扩展高效层聚合网络（E-ELAN）
nodes.label: 架构设计
nodes.summary: 提出E-ELAN架构，通过分组卷积扩展通道和基数，以shuffle和merge方式组合特征，增强学习能力而不破坏原始梯度路径。
nodes.description: E-ELAN在计算块中使用分组卷积来扩展通道和基数，并通过shuffle和merge操作组合不同组的特征，从而在不改变原始梯度传输路径的情况下持续增强网络的学习能力。该设计提高了参数和计算的利用率。

nodes.title: 复合模型缩放方法
nodes.label: 缩放策略
nodes.summary: 针对连接型模型，提出复合缩放方法：缩放计算块的深度和过渡层的宽度，以实现更好的速度-精度权衡。
nodes.description: 对于连接型架构（如PlainNet或ResNet），当进行深度缩放时，计算块的输出宽度也会增加，导致后续传输层输入宽度增加。因此，提出仅缩放计算块的深度，并对传输层进行相应的宽度缩放。实验表明，该方法在参数和计算量增加较少的情况下，AP提升明显。

nodes.title: 计划重参数化模型
nodes.label: 训练优化
nodes.summary: 提出计划重参数化模型，分析RepConv在不同架构中的适用性，避免恒等连接破坏残差或连接操作。
nodes.description: 分析发现，RepConv中的恒等连接会破坏ResNet中的残差和DenseNet中的连接，从而影响梯度多样性。因此，提出计划重参数化模型：在具有残差或连接连接的层中，使用不包含恒等连接的RepConvN。实验在连接型模型（3-stacked ELAN）和残差型模型（CSPDarknet）上验证了有效性。

nodes.title: 粗到细引导标签分配
nodes.label: 标签分配
nodes.summary: 提出粗到细引导标签分配方法，利用主头（lead head）的预测和真值同时为辅助头和主头生成软标签，优化训练。
nodes.description: 针对多输出层模型的动态标签分配问题，提出引导标签分配：使用主头的预测和真值生成软标签，用于训练主头和辅助头。进一步提出粗到细版本：为辅助头生成粗标签（放宽正样本分配约束以优化召回率），为主头生成细标签。该方法使辅助头学习主头已学信息，让主头专注于学习残差信息。

nodes.title: 部分辅助头
nodes.label: 训练优化
nodes.summary: 在E-ELAN架构中设计部分辅助头，连接到合并基数前的一组特征图，以弥补下一级金字塔预测可能丢失的信息。
nodes.description: 由于YOLOv7使用多个金字塔联合预测，将辅助头连接到中间层金字塔可以弥补下一级预测可能丢失的信息。因此，在E-ELAN中设计部分辅助头，连接到合并基数前的一组特征图。实验表明，部分辅助头能进一步提升性能。

nodes.title: 推理时重参数化与EMA
nodes.label: 推理优化
nodes.summary: 在推理阶段，将批归一化层集成到卷积层中，简化YOLOR的隐式知识，并使用EMA模型作为最终推理模型。
nodes.description: 推理时，将批归一化层的均值和方差集成到卷积层的偏置和权重中；将YOLOR的隐式知识简化为向量，并与前一或后一卷积层的偏置和权重结合；使用EMA（指数移动平均）模型作为最终推理模型。这些技术不增加推理成本。

edges.label: 架构影响缩放
edges.description: E-ELAN架构的设计（如连接型结构）直接影响复合缩放方法的制定。

edges.label: 架构支持部分辅助头
edges.description: E-ELAN架构允许在合并基数前连接部分辅助头。

edges.label: 训练重参数化到推理
edges.description: 计划重参数化模型在训练后，推理时通过合并操作实现高效推理。

edges.label: 标签分配指导辅助头训练
edges.description: 粗到细引导标签分配方法为辅助头（包括部分辅助头）提供训练目标。

edges.label: 架构决定重参数化策略
edges.description: E-ELAN等架构的特性（如残差或连接）决定了计划重参数化模型的设计。

deltas.before: 现有模型缩放方法（如仅缩放宽度或深度）在连接型模型上效果不佳。
deltas.after: 提出复合缩放方法：缩放计算块深度（1.5倍）和过渡层宽度（1.25倍）。
deltas.why_it_matters: 在参数和计算量增加较少的情况下，AP提升更明显（如+0.5% AP），实现更好的速度-精度权衡。

deltas.before: 模型重参数化（如RepConv）直接应用于所有层，可能破坏残差或连接操作。
deltas.after: 提出计划重参数化模型：在具有残差或连接连接的层中，使用不包含恒等连接的RepConvN。
deltas.why_it_matters: 避免恒等连接破坏梯度多样性，提升模型性能（如AP提升0.2%）。

deltas.before: 多输出层模型的动态标签分配通常独立处理辅助头和主头。
deltas.after: 提出粗到细引导标签分配：使用主头预测和真值同时生成粗标签（用于辅助头）和细标签（用于主头）。
deltas.why_it_matters: 使辅助头学习主头已学信息，主头专注于残差信息，提升整体检测精度（如AP提升0.3%）。

deltas.before: 辅助头通常连接到网络的中间层，但可能未充分利用多金字塔预测。
deltas.after: 设计部分辅助头，连接到E-ELAN中合并基数前的一组特征图。
deltas.why_it_matters: 弥补下一级金字塔预测可能丢失的信息，进一步提升性能（如AP提升0.5%）。

metadata.title: YOLOv7: Trainable Bag-of-Freebies Sets New State-of-the-Art for Real-Time Object Detectors
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Detection / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: Real-time object detection is one of the most important research topics in computer vision. As new approaches regarding architecture optimization and training optimization are continually being developed, we have found two research topics that have spawned when dealing with these latest state-of-the-art methods. To address the topics, we propose a trainable bag-of-freebies oriented solution. We combine the flexible and efficient training tools with the proposed architecture and the compound scaling method. YOLOv7 surpasses all known object detectors in both speed and accuracy in the range from 5 FPS to 120 FPS and has the highest accuracy 56.8% AP among all known real-time object detectors with 30 FPS or higher on GPU V100. Source code is released in https://github.com/WongKinYiu/yolov7.

anchors.text_span: YOLOv7: Trainable bag-of-freebies sets new state-of-the-art for real-time object detectors Chien-Yao Wang1, Alexey Bochkovskiy, and Hong-Yuan Mark Liao1 1Institute of Information Science, Academia Sinica, Taiwan kinyiu@iis.sinica.edu.tw, alexeyab84@gmail.com, and liao@iis.sinica.edu.tw
Abstract

YOLOv7 surpasses all known object detectors in both speed and accuracy in the range from 5 FPS to 160 FPS and has the highest accuracy 56.8% AP among all known real-time object detectors with 30 FPS or higher on GPU V100. YOLOv7-E6 object detector (56 FPS V100, 55.9% AP) outperforms both transformer-based detector SWIN- L Cascade-Mask R-CNN (9.2 FPS A100, 53.9% AP) by 509% in speed and 2% in accuracy, and convolutional- based detector ConvNeXt-XL Cascade-Mask R-CNN (8.6 FPS A100, 55.2% AP) by 551% in speed and 0.7% AP in accuracy, as well as YOLOv7 outperforms: YOLOR, YOLOX, Scaled-YOLOv4, YOLOv5, DETR, Deformable DETR, DINO-5scale-R50, ViT-Adapter-B and many other object detectors in speed and accuracy. Moreover, we train YOLOv7 only on MS COCO dataset from scratch without using any other datasets or pre-trained weights. Source code is released in https://github.com/WongKinYiu/yolov7. 1. The model re-parameterization technique can be regarded as an en- semble technique, and we can divide it into two cate- gories, i.e., module-level ensemble and model-level ensem- ble. There are two common practices for model-level re- parameterization to obtain the ﬁnal inference model. Model scaling Model scaling [72, 60, 74, 73, 15, 16, 2, 51] is a way to scale up or down an already designed model and make it ﬁt in different computing devices. The model scaling method usually uses different scaling factors, such as reso- lution (size of input image), depth (number of layer), width (number of channel), and stage (number of feature pyra- mid), so as to achieve a good trade-off for the amount of network parameters, computation, inference speed, and ac- curacy. Network architecture search (NAS) is one of the commonly used model scaling methods. NAS can automat- ically search for suitable scaling factors from search space without deﬁning too complicated rules. The disadvantage of NAS is that it requires very expensive computation to complete the search for model scaling factors. Coarse for auxiliary and ﬁne for lead loss Deep supervision [38] is a technique that is often used in training deep networks. Its main concept is to add extra auxiliary head in the middle layers of the network, and the shallow network weights with assistant loss as the guide. Even for architectures such as ResNet [26] and DenseNet [32] which usually converge well, deep supervi- sion [70, 98, 67, 47, 82, 65, 86, 50] can still signiﬁcantly improve the performance of the model on many tasks. During the development of soft label assigner re- lated techniques, we accidentally discovered a new deriva- tive issue, i.e., “How to assign soft label to auxiliary head and lead head ?” To the best of our knowledge, the relevant literature has not explored this issue so far. The results of the most popular method at present is as shown in Figure 5 (c), which is to separate auxiliary head and lead head, and then use their own prediction results and the ground truth to execute label assignment. The method proposed in this paper is a new label assignment method that guides both auxiliary head and lead head by the lead head prediction. In other words, we use lead head prediction as guidance to generate coarse-to-ﬁne hierarchical labels, which are used for auxiliary head and lead head learning, respectively. Conclusions In this paper we propose a new architecture of real- time object detector and the corresponding model scaling method. Furthermore, we ﬁnd that the evolving process of object detection methods generates new research top- ics. During the research process, we found the replace- ment problem of re-parameterized module and the alloca- tion problem of dynamic label assignment. To solve the problem, we propose the trainable bag-of-freebies method to enhance the accuracy of object detection. Based on the above, we have developed the YOLOv7 series of object de- tection systems, which receives the state-of-the-art results. 7.
